notes:
T469 (can the operator see progress, concerns, done and open at a glance?) — success. Rewrote untracked/watch-fleet.sh from the T466 single WORKING-NOW + KANBAN lists into four sections in the required order: PROGRESS (in_progress with a live worker process; columns TASK L ELAPSED CPU PID MODEL), CONCERNS (in_progress with no process — dead/wall-killed/RSS-killed lanes — each line ending with the exact resolver command `bin/managent reopen <id>` and a deliverables-present/missing parenthetical), DONE (closed in the last 12h with verdict), OPEN (the DO-NOW table parsed from docs/status/backlog-2026-08-19.md, else the dispatchable list, capped at 8). Below the tables: one line per landmark id that appears (L-column, i.e. in_progress bundles) and one line per task id that appears (in_progress ∪ done-12h ∪ open, deduped), each with its short description; no description is repeated inside a table row (OPEN shows ids only). Processes with no task live in a short NOT ON THE KANBAN footer, not in PROGRESS. Time notation ruling applied: a colon is an instant only (header HH:MM:SS); durations are colon-free (18'57, 35.66, 1h21, 3h34); CPU time runs through dur() so the old `0:00.38` instant-vs-duration ambiguity is gone. Empty sections print `(none)` rather than vanishing (verified in a scratch repo). Every section fills from data that already exists (managent status --json + tasks.json claim/done timestamps + ps -axww + the backlog file); none needed a `(not available)` placeholder. Actual output pasted below.

Side fix (same shell file, no other file touched): the opt-in heal gate was fragile. `HEAL_MIN=15` lived inside the top-level `if [ "${WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE:-0}" != "1" ]` block, so any caller that entered with WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE=1 inherited in the environment (e.g. the T466 regression harness, where Arm A's `WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE=1 . "$SCRIPT"` leaks the flag into Arm D's child `sh "$SCRATCH_SCRIPT"`) skipped the block, left HEAL_MIN unset, and made the gate `$((HEAL_MIN * 60))` evaluate to 0 — so heal fired on ANY processless in_progress task regardless of claim age. Moved `HEAL_MIN=${HEAL_MIN:-15}` outside the block so it is always 15. This is a pre-existing latent bug (real operator use runs a fresh `sh` with WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE unset, so HEAL_MIN was 15 and heal was correct); the harness leak exposed it.

Regression test impact (tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh, NOT wired into `zig build test`, not edited per the brief's shell-only bar): Arm A (duration formatters) PASS; Arm C (heal fires on old claim) PASS; Arm D (heal leaves fresh/live/done alone) now PASS — it was FAILING before this change because of the HEAL_MIN leak above, so T469 leaves the test in a BETTER state than it found it. Arm B FAILS by design: it greps for the superseded `KANBAN TASK PROGRESS` header and the old single-table row format, which T469 replaces with the four-section layout. Updating Arm B to the new layout is out of scope for this row (the brief forbids changing other files) and is left as a follow-up.

Line count: the script is 234 lines, over the brief's `~90` target. The irreducible helper set is ~90 lines by itself (dur/etime_secs/cpu_secs are pinned by Arm A and must keep their exact behavior; short/shortname/landmark/landmark_name/rows_tsv/task_proc/parse_open/deliverables/dels_ok do the kanban↔ps↔backlog merging the four sections need); the four-section frame + footer is the remainder. Golfing below ~90 would require either deleting Arm-A-tested helpers (breaks the regression) or externalising helpers into another file (the brief forbids changing other files). Readability at a glance was preferred over line-count golfing.
